study.title: Sing to the LORD a new song
study.intro: Psalm 149 calls God's people to celebrate their Maker and King with a new song, dancing, tambourine and harp, because the LORD takes pleasure in His people and crowns the humble with salvation. Then it turns to God's justice: the saints hold His praises in their mouths and a sword in their hands to carry out the judgment written against oppressive nations. For Christians, this points to the spiritual battle and to Christ's final judgment, not to taking up arms.
study.context: Psalm 149 may come from a festival celebrating victory or the restoration of Jerusalem. The 'judgment written' (verse 9) refers to judgments already decreed in Scripture against nations that oppressed God's people. In the New Testament, the sword becomes the word of God (Ephesians 6:17; Hebrews 4:12), and final judgment belongs to Christ (Revelation 19:11-16). Believers are told not to avenge themselves (Romans 12:19).
study.peopleNote: No author is named. The godly, the children of Zion and the saints are God's people. Kings and nobles of the nations appear as oppressors under judgment. God is never portrayed as a human figure in planned art, and no violence is depicted.

verses.title: A new song in the assembly
verses.heading: His praise in the assembly of the godly
verses.meaning: 'Hallelujah! Sing to the LORD a new song—His praise in the assembly of the godly.' God's people are called to sing a new song together. A new song celebrates fresh mercies and new acts of God. And it is sung in the assembly, the gathered community. Worship is not only private; there is special joy in praising God together with His people.
verses.context: Psalm 96:1 says sing to the LORD a new song. Psalm 22:22 says, 'I will praise You in the assembly.' Hebrews 10:25 urges believers not to neglect meeting together.
explore: New song
A fresh song of praise celebrating something new God has done.
Assembly of the godly
The gathered community of God's faithful people worshiping together.
verses.reflect: What new mercy could you celebrate with God's people this week?
verses.alt: A crowd of worshipers singing together in a sunlit courtyard.

verses.title: Rejoice in Maker and King
verses.heading: Let Israel rejoice in their Maker
verses.meaning: 'Let Israel rejoice in their Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King.' God is both Maker and King. He created His people and He rules over them. Both are reasons to rejoice. We belong to the One who made us on purpose and who leads us with love. Joy in God flows from knowing who He is to us.
verses.context: Isaiah 43:1 says, 'This is what the LORD says—He who created you, O Jacob, and He who formed you, O Israel.' Zechariah 9:9 says, 'Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem! See, your King comes to you.' Psalm 95:6 calls us to kneel before the LORD our Maker.
explore: Maker
Creator, the One who formed His people and gave them life.
Children of Zion
The people of Jerusalem and, more broadly, all God's people.
verses.reflect: How does knowing God is both your Maker and your King bring you joy?
verses.alt: Children dancing in a city street as people cheer around them.

verses.title: Dancing and tambourines
verses.heading: Praise His name with dancing
verses.meaning: 'Let them praise His name with dancing, and make music to Him with tambourine and harp.' Praise involves the whole body. Dancing, tambourines and harps express joy that cannot stay still. Israel celebrated God's victories this way, as Miriam did after the Red Sea. Worship can be joyful, physical and loud as well as quiet and reverent.
verses.context: Exodus 15:20 says Miriam took a tambourine and all the women followed her dancing. 2 Samuel 6:14 says David danced before the LORD with all his might. Psalm 150:4 says praise Him with tambourine and dancing.
explore: Tambourine
A hand drum with jingles, often played by women in celebrations.
Dancing
Moving the body in rhythm to music, an expression of joy in worship.
verses.reflect: How might you express joy to God with your whole body?
verses.alt: Women playing tambourines and dancing by a lakeshore.

verses.title: God delights in His people
verses.heading: The LORD takes pleasure in His people
verses.meaning: 'For the LORD takes pleasure in His people; He adorns the afflicted with salvation.' Here is why we rejoice: God delights in us. He is not reluctant or disappointed; He takes pleasure in His people. And He crowns the humble and afflicted with salvation, like dressing them in beautiful garments. The lowly are honored by God.
verses.context: Zephaniah 3:17 says God will rejoice over you with singing. Isaiah 61:3 says He gives a crown of beauty instead of ashes. Isaiah 62:5 says as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so will your God rejoice over you.
explore: Takes pleasure
Delights in and enjoys, finding real joy and gladness in someone.
Adorns
Decorates or clothes beautifully, here with the gift of salvation.
verses.reflect: How does knowing God takes pleasure in you change how you see yourself?
verses.alt: A woman placing a flower wreath on a smiling child's head.

verses.title: Joy upon their beds
verses.heading: Let the saints exult in glory
verses.meaning: 'Let the saints exult in glory; let them shout for joy upon their beds.' Joy is not limited to public worship. Even lying in bed at night, God's people can rejoice. The bed might be a place of rest, sickness or sleeplessness, yet there too God's glory can fill the heart with song. Worship can happen anywhere.
verses.context: Psalm 63:6 says, 'When I remember You on my bed, I think of You through the watches of the night.' Job 35:10 speaks of God who gives songs in the night. Acts 16:25 tells of Paul and Silas singing at midnight in prison.
explore: Exult
To rejoice greatly and triumphantly, celebrating with great joy.
Upon their beds
In their beds at night, a place of rest, privacy or even sickness.
verses.reflect: Could you praise God tonight before you sleep? What would you thank Him for?
verses.alt: A small bedroom with moonlight through a window and a person resting peacefully.

verses.title: Praise and a sword
verses.heading: A double-edged sword in their hands
verses.meaning: 'May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a double-edged sword in their hands,' Praise and battle are joined. In Nehemiah's day, builders worked with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other. For Christians, the sword becomes God's word, our weapon in spiritual battle. Praise and Scripture go together as we stand against evil.
verses.context: Nehemiah 4:17 describes builders working with one hand and holding a weapon with the other. Ephesians 6:17 calls the word of God the sword of the Spirit. Hebrews 4:12 says God's word is sharper than any double-edged sword.
explore: High praises
Exalted praise lifted up loudly to God with the whole heart.
Double-edged sword
A sword sharpened on both sides; in the New Testament a picture of God's word.
verses.reflect: How can praise and God's word help you stand against evil today?
verses.alt: A scroll and a lyre resting together on a stone bench at dawn.

verses.title: Justice on the nations
verses.heading: To inflict vengeance on the nations
verses.meaning: 'to inflict vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples,' This verse speaks of God's justice against nations that oppressed His people. In Israel's history, God sometimes used His people to bring judgment. But the New Testament makes clear that vengeance belongs to God alone, and final judgment will be carried out by Christ. Believers fight with spiritual weapons, not violence.
verses.context: Deuteronomy 32:35 and Romans 12:19 say, 'Vengeance is Mine; I will repay.' 2 Corinthians 10:4 says the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh. Revelation 19:11-16 pictures Christ judging with justice.
explore: Vengeance
Punishment for wrongdoing; in Scripture, God's right to bring justice.
Nations
Peoples outside Israel, here those who opposed and oppressed God's people.
verses.reflect: How does trusting God with justice free you from seeking revenge?
verses.alt: Storm clouds rolling over a distant fortress city at dusk.

verses.title: Kings in chains
verses.heading: To bind their kings with chains
verses.meaning: 'to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with shackles of iron,' Proud rulers who oppressed God's people would be humbled. The powerful who bound others would themselves be bound. This pictures God's justice reversing the order of the world. Jesus spoke of binding the strong man, Satan, and setting captives free.
verses.context: Matthew 12:29 speaks of binding the strong man before plundering his house. Isaiah 45:14 pictures nations coming in chains to acknowledge God. Revelation 20:2 describes Satan bound with a great chain.
explore: Shackles
Iron rings or chains fastened around the wrists or ankles of prisoners.
Nobles
Important officials and aristocrats who held power with kings.
verses.reflect: What powers of evil do you trust Christ to bind and defeat?
verses.alt: Broken iron chains lying on palace steps.

verses.title: Honor for all the saints
verses.heading: This honor is for all His saints
verses.meaning: 'to execute the judgment written against them. This honor is for all His saints. Hallelujah!' The judgment is already 'written' in God's word; His people simply share in carrying out His decree. To be part of God's victory over evil is an honor for all His saints. Paul says believers will one day share in judging the world. The psalm ends, again, with Hallelujah.
verses.context: 1 Corinthians 6:2 says the saints will judge the world. Revelation 2:26 promises authority over the nations to those who overcome. Daniel 7:22 says judgment was given in favor of the saints.
explore: Judgment written
The verdicts God has already recorded in Scripture against evil and oppression.
Saints
God's faithful, holy people, those set apart as His own.
verses.reflect: How does sharing in Christ's victory give you dignity and hope?
verses.alt: A crowd of worshipers raising palm branches in a sunlit courtyard.
